title: Span Relationship Map + Filter Rail: prototype for connected-span visualization
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and prototype a new trace-level exploration view: the Span Relationship Map combined with a persistent Filter Rail. Goal: give engineers a graph-first way to understand span relationships, repeated correlation IDs, and cross-request dependencies while keeping timeline context for latency hotspots. This is intended to complement the existing timeline/span list views (not replace them) and to support quick triage flows (pin spans, compare durations, open raw payloads).
acceptance_criteria: Interactive Figma prototype linked and walkthrough recorded
Engineers sign off on virtualized canvas approach for >1000 spans
PM approves prioritization and mapping of rollout flags
Accessibility keyboard flows documented for node selection and filter rail
A/B plan for opt-in beta with 5 customers defined
design_decisions: Primary node layout: time-aware force layout where x-axis maps to request time and y-axis groups service/host
Filter Rail: persistent right-side panel with quick facets (correlation id, status, duration buckets, tags) and saved filter presets
Pin & Compare: users can pin up to 3 spans; compare pane shows per-span token counts, latency breakdowns, and first-byte vs tail latency
Fallbacks: when span count > 1000 default to aggregated view with rollup nodes; provide table-export of raw spans
Performance trade-off: use canvas + webgl rendering for nodes; provide accessible HTML list mirror for screen readers
